content:
My most sincere advice here is to just ignore the z-axis calibration. Complete it in a way that makes the printer happy. But completing this calibration step is in no way a guarantee that the wiper is properly calibrated.

What worked for me was just to start a print and let the printer yell at me if the nozzle was not clean, then retry the print while making small adjustments to the knob using the wrench. Eventually I got to a point that worked, no thanks to the calibration step here.

Prusa really needs a better solution here. One thing that I think would help would be for this calibration step to actually extrude some filament to verify that the wiper is working.
I don't think this is current. Mine didn't ever ask me to put it in the grove in the bin. I did it twice. It seemed like it just probed the bin with the nozzle tip.

As jetuser said, this needs better images both in the printer firmware and here as well.

This will affect your every print (and nozzle changes) as the print won't start if the nozzle has even - and I'm not joking - a tiny drop of filament in tip of it (the tool offset will fail during print startup).
I think the picture for the Z-Alignment could use improvement, to better illustrate expected nozzle pressure/placement in the v groove wiper
